title: Eminem and Elvis vs. the $5.4 Billion AI Song App
alt_title_1: Why Eminem's Publisher Wants $41 Million From Suno
alt_title_2: The AI App That Learned From Almost Every Song Online
description_hook: On November 6, 2026, Eminem's publisher Eight Mile Style and the owners of Elvis Presley's catalog filed separate lawsuits against Suno, an AI music app valued at $5.4 billion. These are allegations; no court has ruled.

affiliate_cta.offer_name: Free 48-Case Lawsuit & Refund Dossier + Forensics Reading List
affiliate_cta.pinned_comment: Should AI companies pay for the songs they learn from? Sources for every number in this video are in the description.

scenes.headline: Eminem's Publisher Wants $41 Million
scenes.narration: Eminem's publisher wants 41 million dollars from an AI app.

scenes.headline: Then Elvis Sued Too
scenes.narration: The same night, Elvis Presley's catalog owners sued too.

scenes.headline: Trained on Almost Every Song Online
scenes.narration: The lawsuit quotes Suno's own words: its AI learned from essentially all music of reasonable quality on the open internet.
scenes.source: Eight Mile Style v. Suno, No. 3:26-cv-13399 (N.D. Cal.)

scenes.headline: A $5.4 Billion Company
scenes.narration: That music helped build a 5.4 billion dollar company. The songwriters got nothing, the suit says.
scenes.source: Suno blog, Jun 3, 2026; complaint via Detroit Free Press, Nov 7, 2026

scenes.headline: Owners Set the Price
scenes.left_body: Valued at $5.4B. Says training is fair use
scenes.right_body: Hold the rights, so they set the price
scenes.narration: No court has ruled yet. But the rule is old: whoever owns the asset sets the price, even against a billion dollar machine.
